bank_metadata.edge_case_policy: Each question includes five representative, problem-specific edge cases. This is comprehensive test coverage, not exhaustive enumeration of all possible inputs.
bank_metadata.deduplication_note: All 100 question IDs are unique and there are no exact title collisions between batches; problem designs were reviewed for intentional overlap.

questions.title: Count Positive Elements
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return the number of elements strictly greater than zero. Zero is not positive.
questions.output_format: An integer count.

examples.explanation: Only 4 and 7 are strictly positive.
Every element is positive.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No elements should be counted.
Zero is excluded by the strict comparison.
Negative values are not positive.
The final index must be examined.
The full allowed numeric range must work.

questions.title: Second Largest Distinct Value
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return its second-largest distinct value. Return null when fewer than two distinct values exist.
questions.output_format: The second-largest distinct integer, or null.

examples.explanation: The distinct values in descending order begin with 8 and 5.
-2 is largest and -7 is second largest.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no distinct values.
One distinct value is insufficient.
Duplicates do not create a second distinct value.
The answer must be distinct from the maximum.
Ordering must work for negative integers.

questions.title: Rotate Array Left
questions.problem_statement: Given an array nums and a non-negative integer k, rotate the array left by k positions. Return the rotated array. Rotating an empty array returns an empty array.
questions.output_format: A new array containing nums rotated left by k positions.

examples.explanation: The first two elements move to the end.
One left rotation shifts the first element to the end.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: Avoid modulo by zero and return an empty result.
A zero rotation preserves the array.
A full-length rotation is the identity.

edge_cases.case: Rotation count much larger than length
edge_cases.why_it_matters: The effective rotation is k modulo n.
A one-element array never changes.

questions.title: Move Zeroes to the End
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, move every zero to the end while preserving the relative order of all non-zero elements. Modify the array in place and return it.
questions.output_format: The modified array with non-zero elements in original order followed by all zeroes.

examples.explanation: Non-zero values retain their original order.
Negative non-zero values remain in sequence.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The operation must safely handle no elements.
The input should remain unchanged.
All elements belong at the end.
The relative order of non-zero values must be preserved.
A one-element zero array is unchanged.

questions.title: Longest Run of Ones
questions.problem_statement: Given a binary array nums, return the length of the longest contiguous run of 1s.
questions.output_format: The maximum length of a contiguous run of ones.

examples.explanation: The final run contains three consecutive ones.
The entire array is one run.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There is no run in an empty input.
No ones are present.
Each one forms a run of length one.
A singleton one is a run of length one.
The final run must be considered without a trailing zero.

questions.title: Transpose a Rectangular Matrix
questions.problem_statement: Given an m by n matrix, return its transpose. The transpose has n rows and m columns, with element (i, j) equal to the original element (j, i). An empty matrix returns an empty matrix.
questions.output_format: A new matrix representing the transpose.
constraints: If m is zero, matrix is []

examples.explanation: Rows become columns.
A one-row matrix becomes a one-column matrix.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no rows to transpose.
The output must contain one single-element row per input value.
A column becomes a row.
A 1 by 1 matrix is unchanged.
Values must be copied without alteration.

questions.title: Sum of Both Matrix Diagonals
questions.problem_statement: Given a square integer matrix, return the sum of its primary diagonal and secondary diagonal. If the matrix has odd size, count the center cell only once.
questions.output_format: A single integer diagonal sum.

examples.explanation: The diagonal cells sum to 1+5+9+3+7; the center is counted once.
For even n, the two diagonals do not overlap.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The sole cell belongs to both diagonals but is counted once.
Zero diagonal values contribute nothing.
The shared center must not be double-counted.
Both diagonal positions are distinct.
The sum must support cancellation at constraint limits.

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
questions.problem_statement: Given two non-decreasing integer arrays a and b, return one non-decreasing array containing every element from both inputs, including duplicates.
questions.output_format: A merged non-decreasing integer array.

examples.explanation: The two sorted sequences are merged in order.
Duplicates from both inputs are retained.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No values are available.
The non-empty input is already the result.
All duplicate occurrences must be retained.
All of one sequence may precede the other.
Ordering must include negative integers.

questions.title: Find the Missing Number
questions.problem_statement: An array nums contains n distinct integers chosen from the range [0, n]. Return the single number in that range that is missing.

input_format.nums: n distinct integers from 0 through n, with one missing

questions.output_format: The missing integer.

examples.explanation: The range is 0 through 3 and 2 is absent.
The missing value is between present values.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: For n=0, the range contains only zero.
The lower endpoint may be missing.
The upper endpoint n may be missing.
Small ranges must be handled exactly.
The input is not guaranteed to be sorted.

questions.title: First Index at Least Target
questions.problem_statement: Given a non-decreasing integer array nums and an integer target, return the first index i such that nums[i] is greater than or equal to target. Return nums.length if no such index exists.
questions.output_format: The lower-bound index in the range [0, nums.length].

examples.explanation: Index 1 is the first occurrence that is not below 2.
The first value at least 4 is 5 at index 2.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The insertion point in an empty array is zero.
The lower bound is the first index.
The result can equal the array length.
The first qualifying duplicate must be returned.
Comparison must work across negative values.

questions.title: Product of Array Except Self
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer where answer[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i]. Do not use division. Assume every output fits in a signed 64-bit integer.
questions.output_format: An integer array of the same length containing products excluding each position.
constraints: Every required product fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: Each output is the product of the other three values.
A single zero makes all products except at its position zero.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: Only the zero's position has a non-zero product.
Every excluded product still contains a zero.
Sign changes must be correct.
Identity values must not affect products.
Intermediate multiplication must use sufficient precision.

questions.title: Maximum Subarray Sum
questions.problem_statement: Given a non-empty integer array nums, find the contiguous non-empty subarray with the largest sum and return that sum.
questions.output_format: The maximum sum over all non-empty contiguous subarrays.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has sum 6.
The entire array has the maximum sum.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: A non-empty subarray is required; zero is not a valid answer.
The only possible subarray contains the single value.
The best subarray may contain one element.
Any non-empty subarray has sum zero.
The running sum must avoid 32-bit overflow.

questions.title: Count Subarrays With Sum K
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays whose elements sum exactly to k.
questions.output_format: An integer count of qualifying subarrays.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The two length-two subarrays each sum to 2.
The qualifying subarrays are [1,-1], [0], and [1,-1,0].

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no non-empty subarrays.
A single-element subarray can qualify.
Every contiguous non-empty segment qualifies.
Negative numbers invalidate sliding-window-only assumptions.
The function must return zero when no segment matches.

questions.title: Sort an Array of Three Colors
questions.problem_statement: Given an array nums containing only 0, 1, and 2, sort it in non-decreasing order in place. Do not use a library sorting function.
questions.output_format: The sorted array [all 0s, then all 1s, then all 2s].

examples.explanation: Values are grouped in ascending order.
One occurrence of each color is sorted.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No partition steps should access an element.
An already uniform array remains unchanged.
Every partition boundary must move correctly.
The middle category may be absent.
A singleton is already sorted.

questions.title: Spiral Matrix Traversal
questions.problem_statement: Given an m by n matrix, return all elements in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner. An empty matrix returns an empty list.
questions.output_format: A one-dimensional list containing each matrix element exactly once in spiral order.

examples.explanation: Traverse top, right, bottom, then left while shrinking boundaries.
A single row is traversed once.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no rows.
A single column must not be revisited.
The only cell is emitted exactly once.
The bottom boundary must be traversed in reverse.
Boundary updates must work when height exceeds width.

questions.title: Set Matrix Rows and Columns to Zero
questions.problem_statement: Given an m by n integer matrix, if any cell is zero, set every cell in that cell's row and column to zero. Perform the transformation in place using O(1) auxiliary space.
questions.output_format: The modified matrix after all required rows and columns are zeroed.

examples.explanation: The zero at the center clears its full row and column.
The first row and first column are cleared.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: First-row and first-column markers overlap.
The matrix must remain unchanged.
The result remains all zeroes.
A zero clears the only row.
A zero clears the only column.

questions.title: Longest Consecutive Integer Run
questions.problem_statement: Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the length of the longest set of consecutive integer values. Values need not be adjacent in the original array, and duplicates do not extend a run.
questions.output_format: The maximum number of distinct consecutive values present.

examples.explanation: The values 1, 2, 3, and 4 form the longest run.
The distinct values -1, 0, and 1 form a run.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No sequence exists.
A single value forms a sequence of length one.
Duplicates count once.
Consecutive runs may cross negative values.
Neighbor checks must not assume a narrow value range.

questions.title: Count Subarrays With Sum Divisible by K
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and a positive integer k, count non-empty contiguous subarrays whose sum is divisible by k. Negative values are allowed.
questions.output_format: The number of qualifying subarrays.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: Seven contiguous subarrays have sums divisible by five.
The one-element sum is divisible by five.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No non-empty subarrays exist.
Every integer sum is divisible by one.
Remainders must be normalized for negative sums.
Every subarray sum is zero.
No non-empty segment reaches a nonzero multiple of k.

questions.title: Rotate Square Matrix Clockwise
questions.problem_statement: Given an n by n matrix, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise in place. Do not allocate another n by n matrix.
questions.output_format: The same matrix after a 90-degree clockwise rotation.

examples.explanation: The first column becomes the first row in reverse row order.
The four corners rotate clockwise.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: A 1 by 1 matrix is unchanged.
Small layer rotation must preserve all four cells.
Equal values can hide incorrect movement but result stays unchanged.
Values must move without sign changes.
The center cell remains in its central position.

questions.title: Three Sum Unique Triplets
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return all unique triplets [a,b,c] whose values come from three different indices and satisfy a+b+c=0. The result must not contain duplicate triplets; each triplet should be internally sorted, and result order may be arbitrary.
questions.output_format: A list of unique zero-sum triplets.

examples.explanation: There are two distinct value triplets that sum to zero.
Repeated indices can produce one unique value triplet.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No triple sums to zero.
The only possible triplet qualifies.
Duplicate value combinations must be emitted once.
Only one unique zero triplet exists.
The sum calculation must be performed without narrow-integer overflow.

questions.expected_space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space excluding sorting and output

questions.title: Maximum Water Container Area
questions.problem_statement: Given an array height where height[i] is a non-negative vertical line height at position i, choose two lines that, with the x-axis, contain the most water. Return the maximum area. The width is the index difference.
questions.output_format: The maximum container area as an integer.

examples.explanation: Lines at indices 1 and 8 give width 7 and height 7.
The only pair has width one and height one.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: Every possible container has zero area.
There is exactly one candidate pair.
The shorter endpoint limits each candidate area.
The widest pair need not use adjacent lines.
Area calculations must use a sufficiently wide numeric type.

questions.title: Next Lexicographical Permutation
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, rearrange it into the next lexicographically greater permutation. If no greater permutation exists, rearrange it into ascending order. Modify nums in place and return it.

input_format.nums: Integer array representing a permutation with possible duplicate values

questions.output_format: The next lexicographical arrangement, or the smallest arrangement if the input is maximal.

examples.explanation: The next permutation after [1,2,3] is [1,3,2].
The descending arrangement is maximal, so wrap to ascending order.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There is only one arrangement.
The only greater permutation swaps the values.
A maximal permutation wraps to the minimum.
Duplicate values still follow lexicographical ordering.
The pivot and smallest larger suffix value must be chosen correctly.

questions.title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
questions.problem_statement: Given a collection of closed intervals [start,end], merge all intervals that overlap or touch at an endpoint. Return the resulting intervals sorted by start.
questions.output_format: A list of pairwise non-overlapping intervals sorted by start.

examples.explanation: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap and merge.
Closed intervals sharing endpoint 4 overlap.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no intervals to return.
A single interval is unchanged.
Disjoint intervals must remain separate.
Contained intervals do not extend the outer interval.
Sorting and overlap checks must work with negative values.

questions.title: Find the Repeated Number
questions.problem_statement: An array nums of length n+1 contains integers in the range [1,n]. Exactly one distinct value is repeated one or more times; all other values appear exactly once. Return the repeated value without modifying nums and using O(1) extra space.

input_format.nums: Array of length n+1 with values in [1,n]

questions.output_format: The duplicated integer.
constraints: Exactly one distinct value is duplicated

examples.explanation: The value 2 occurs twice.
The value 3 is the repeated value.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The smallest domain has one repeated value.
The repeated value may occur more than twice.
The maximum permitted value can be duplicated.
The algorithm cannot depend on sorted input.
The minimum allowed value can be repeated.

questions.title: Kth Largest Element
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element when values are ordered with duplicates included. Do not fully sort the array as the required approach target is average O(n).
questions.output_format: The kth largest value, counting duplicate occurrences.

examples.explanation: The sorted descending values begin 6, 5.
Duplicates occupy separate ranks.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The first largest rank is the maximum.
The final rank is the minimum.
Every rank has the same value.
Descending order among negatives must be correct.
Repeated maximum values must occupy separate positions.

questions.expected_space_complexity: O(1) average for in-place quickselect; O(n) worst-case depending on strategy

questions.title: Search a Row-and-Column Sorted Matrix
questions.problem_statement: Given an m by n matrix where each row is non-decreasing from left to right and each column is non-decreasing from top to bottom, determine whether target exists in the matrix.

input_format.matrix: Rectangular matrix sorted by rows and columns

questions.output_format: A boolean indicating whether target occurs in the matrix.

examples.explanation: 6 is present in the third row, second column.
7 is not present.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The only cell matches.
The only cell does not match.
The search boundary should terminate correctly.
The search must not run past the matrix.
Finding any occurrence is sufficient.

questions.title: Count Subarrays With XOR K
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays whose bitwise XOR equals k. Treat values as non-negative integers.
questions.output_format: The number of qualifying contiguous subarrays.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: Four contiguous ranges have XOR equal to 6.
The two length-two subarrays have XOR zero.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No non-empty subarray exists.
The one element is a qualifying subarray.
Every contiguous segment has XOR zero.
The count is zero when no prefix pair qualifies.
Bitwise operations must preserve the full 31-bit non-negative values.

questions.title: Maximum Product Subarray
questions.problem_statement: Given a non-empty integer array nums, find the contiguous non-empty subarray with the largest product and return that product. Products fit in signed 64-bit range.
questions.output_format: The maximum contiguous subarray product.
constraints: Every candidate product fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The subarray [2,3] has product 6.
The zero is larger than either negative singleton product.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: A non-empty subarray is required.
The single value is the only product.
The product of two negatives is positive.
A zero resets the running product segment.
Both maximum and minimum ending products may be needed.

questions.title: Find All Right-Side Leaders
questions.problem_statement: An element nums[i] is a leader if it is strictly greater than every element to its right. The final element is always a leader. Return all leaders in their original left-to-right order.
questions.output_format: An array containing the leader values in original order.

examples.explanation: 17, 5, and the final value 2 exceed every value to their right.
Every element is a leader in a strictly decreasing array.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The final element is always a leader.
Only the final maximum is a leader.
Strict comparison excludes the first 5 because an equal value is to its right.
Only the final equal element qualifies.
Comparisons must work for negative values.

questions.title: Maximum Sum of a Fixed-Length Subarray
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the maximum sum among all contiguous subarrays of exactly k elements.
questions.output_format: The largest sum of any length-k contiguous subarray.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The window [5,1,3] has the maximum sum 9.
The window [-3,-1] has the largest sum.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There is exactly one candidate window.
The answer is the maximum single element.
The algorithm must not default to zero.
Several windows share the same best sum.
Window sums need a wide integer type.

questions.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
questions.problem_statement: Given two non-decreasing arrays a and b, return the median of the combined multiset. The combined length is at least one. If the total length is even, return the arithmetic mean of the two middle values. The target time complexity is O(log(min(n,m)+1)).
questions.output_format: The median as a number; it may end in .5.

examples.explanation: The combined sequence is [1,2,3].
The middle values are 2 and 3.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The median comes entirely from the second array.
A single non-empty array is valid.
The only element is the median.
The partition search must handle very different lengths.
Equal partition values must not break binary search.

questions.title: Trapping Rain Water
questions.problem_statement: Given an array height of non-negative bar heights, compute how much water can be trapped after raining. Each bar has width one.
questions.output_format: The total trapped water as an integer.
constraints: The result fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The elevations form several basins that hold six units in total.
The bounded valleys hold nine units.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no bars.
Two bars cannot enclose a positive-width interior basin.
No right boundary traps water above an interior bar.
No left boundary creates a basin.
Both interior positions trap water up to height five.

questions.title: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram
questions.problem_statement: Given an array heights where each bar has width one and non-negative height, return the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed using one or more consecutive bars.
questions.output_format: The maximum rectangle area.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: Bars of heights 5 and 6 form a width-two rectangle of area 10.
The taller bar alone gives area 4.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No rectangle can be formed.
Every rectangle has zero area.
The only bar forms the best rectangle.
The best rectangle may end before the final bar.
Equal bars combine into a wider rectangle.

questions.title: Maximal Rectangle of Ones
questions.problem_statement: Given a matrix of characters '0' and '1', find the area of the largest axis-aligned rectangle containing only '1' cells. Return zero for an empty matrix.

input_format.matrix: Rectangular character matrix containing only '0' and '1'

questions.output_format: The maximum all-ones rectangle area.
constraints: If m is zero, matrix is []

examples.explanation: The largest all-ones rectangle has three rows and two columns.
The entire 2 by 2 matrix is filled with ones.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No cells exist.
A zero cell cannot belong to a valid rectangle.
One cell forms a rectangle of area one.
No all-ones rectangle exists.
The answer can be a one-row rectangle.

questions.title: First Missing Positive Integer
questions.problem_statement: Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the smallest positive integer that does not appear in nums. The algorithm must run in O(n) time and use O(1) extra space by modifying the array in place.
questions.output_format: The smallest missing positive integer.

examples.explanation: 1 and 2 are present, so 3 is missing.
The smallest missing positive is 2.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: One is the smallest positive absent value.
No positive value is present.
The answer follows the complete present prefix.
Duplicate values must not cause placement loops.
Values greater than n cannot occupy useful answer positions.

questions.title: Shortest Subarray With Sum At Least K
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, which may contain negative values, and an integer k, return the length of the shortest non-empty contiguous subarray whose sum is at least k. Return -1 if no such subarray exists.

input_format.nums: Integer array, possibly containing negative values

questions.output_format: The shortest qualifying length, or -1.
constraints: Prefix sums fit in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The whole array sums to 3 and no shorter segment reaches 3.
The segment [32,40,95] sums to 167.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No non-empty segment exists.
A single element can meet the threshold.
No subarray reaches the threshold.
The best qualifying range can include a negative value.
A negative or zero threshold still requires a non-empty segment.

questions.title: Count Range-Sum Subarrays
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and integers lower and upper, count non-empty contiguous subarrays whose sum lies in the inclusive range [lower, upper]. The target time complexity is O(n log n).
questions.output_format: The number of qualifying subarrays.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The qualifying subarray sums are -2, 1, and -1.
All three non-empty subarrays have sum zero.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no non-empty subarrays.
Only the first element sums to exactly four.
Every non-empty subarray qualifies.
Inclusive negative sum bounds must be respected.
No subarray reaches the lower bound.

questions.function_signature: countRangeSum(nums: integer[], lower: integer, upper: integer) -> integer

questions.title: Count Important Reverse Pairs
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, count pairs (i,j) such that i < j and nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]. The comparison must be evaluated without integer overflow. The target time complexity is O(n log n).
questions.output_format: The number of important reverse pairs.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: The qualifying pairs are (3,1) at two positions.
Three index pairs satisfy the strict doubled comparison.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no index pairs.
A pair requires two indices.
2 is not strictly greater than 2*1.
-5 is greater than 2*(-3), so signed comparisons matter.
Doubling the second value must not overflow a 32-bit integer.

questions.title: Split Array to Minimize Largest Segment Sum
questions.problem_statement: Given a non-empty array of non-negative integers nums and an integer m, split nums into exactly m non-empty contiguous parts. Minimize the largest part sum and return that minimum possible value.

input_format.m: Required number of non-empty contiguous parts

questions.output_format: The minimum achievable maximum segment sum.
constraints: The answer fits in signed 64-bit range

examples.explanation: Splitting [7,2,5] and [10,8] gives largest sum 18, which is optimal.
The split [1,2,3] and [4,5] has maximum sum 9.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The entire array must stay together.
The maximum part sum is the largest element.
Every possible segment sum is zero.
The answer may be dominated by a single element.

edge_cases.case: Each element in its own part
edge_cases.why_it_matters: Exactly two non-empty zero-sum parts are required.

questions.title: Maximum Sum Rectangle No Larger Than K
questions.problem_statement: Given a non-empty m by n integer matrix and an integer k, find the maximum sum of any non-empty axis-aligned rectangular submatrix whose sum is less than or equal to k. It is guaranteed that at least one rectangle has sum <= k.
questions.output_format: The largest rectangle sum that does not exceed k.

examples.explanation: The best rectangle with sum at most two has sum 2.
The whole row sums to 3.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The only rectangle qualifies and gives the answer.
The best permitted sum may be negative.
A rectangle equal to k must be accepted.
Rectangles may span a row subset only.
Rectangles may span a column subset only.

questions.title: Count Smaller Values After Each Element
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return an array counts where counts[i] is the number of elements strictly smaller than nums[i] that appear to its right. Equal values are not counted.
questions.output_format: An integer array of counts with the same length as nums.

examples.explanation: To the right of 5 are 2 and 1; to the right of 2 is 1; to the right of 6 is 1.
Equal values are not strictly smaller.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There are no positions to count.
No elements follow the final position.
No value to the right is smaller.
Every later value is smaller.
Equality must not be counted.

questions.title: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and a window size k, slide a window of length k from left to right. Return the maximum value in each window.
questions.output_format: An array containing one maximum per window.

examples.explanation: Each output is the maximum of a consecutive length-three window.
A size-one window returns each element.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There is exactly one window.
Every element is its own window maximum.
Duplicate maximums must be handled consistently.
The maximum leaves the window at each step.
The algorithm must not assume non-negative values.

questions.title: Maximum Sum of Three Non-Overlapping Windows
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and a positive window length k, choose three non-overlapping subarrays, each of length k, to maximize their total sum. Return their starting indices in increasing order. If multiple choices have the same maximum sum, return the lexicographically smallest index triple.

input_format.k: Common positive length of the three windows

questions.output_format: Three starting indices [i,j,l] with i+k <= j and j+k <= l.

examples.explanation: The windows [1,2], [2,6], and [7,5] total 23.
All valid triples tie, so the lexicographically smallest is selected.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: Exactly three disjoint singleton windows fit.
The maximum is still defined when every window sum is negative.
Tie-breaking must choose the earliest lexicographic triple.
Chosen windows must be non-overlapping even when peaks overlap.
Sum calculations must use wide integer precision.

questions.title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array arr, compute the sum of the minimum value of every non-empty contiguous subarray. Return the result modulo 1,000,000,007. Duplicate values must be assigned consistently so each subarray is counted exactly once.
questions.output_format: The sum of all subarray minimums modulo 1,000,000,007.

examples.explanation: The subarray minima sum to 3+1+1+1+2+1+2+4+1+2.
The sum of all contiguous-subarray minimums is 444.

questions.output_format: The maximum total reward collected by the two robots.

examples.explanation: An optimal pair of paths collects 24 while counting a shared cell only once.
The robots collect 1 and 2 on the first row, then 3 and 4 on the second row.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: Both robots start in the same cell, which must be counted once.
The robots necessarily share the only cell in each row.
Each robot collects its starting endpoint and no movement occurs.
Every valid pair of paths has total reward zero.
The best paths can collect the center 9 once and collect one additional side cell in that row.

questions.title: Minimum Cost to Merge K Consecutive Piles
questions.problem_statement: Given positive pile weights stones and an integer k, one operation merges exactly k consecutive piles into one pile whose weight is their sum; the operation cost equals that sum. Return the minimum total cost to merge all piles into one, or -1 if it is impossible.

input_format.k: Number of consecutive piles merged per operation

questions.output_format: The minimum total merge cost, or -1 when no complete merge is possible.

examples.explanation: Merging 3+2, then 4+1, then the two resulting piles costs 5+5+10=20.
With k=3, the pile count cannot be reduced from four to one.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No merge is needed.
There are not enough consecutive piles to perform an operation.
All piles merge in one operation costing their total weight.
The only operation merges the two piles.
Every merge choice must preserve the required consecutive-pile rule.

questions.title: Smallest Range Covering Elements From K Sorted Lists
questions.problem_statement: You are given k non-empty lists, each sorted in non-decreasing order. Find the smallest inclusive interval [low, high] that contains at least one element from every list. Minimize interval width; if widths tie, choose the interval with the smaller low endpoint.

input_format.lists: List of k non-empty non-decreasing integer arrays

questions.output_format: A two-element array [low, high] describing the selected interval.

examples.explanation: The interval [20,24] contains 24, 20, and 22 from the three lists.
The same value from all lists gives a zero-width range.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: Any one element covers the only list; the smallest low-tie interval uses its minimum.
The interval must span all singleton values.
Equal values can create a zero-width range.
The optimal interval [-10,-8] includes one value from each list.
When widths tie, the smaller low endpoint wins.

questions.title: Minimum Swaps to Make Two Sequences Strictly Increasing
questions.problem_statement: You are given two integer arrays A and B of equal length. At any index, you may swap A[i] with B[i]. Return the minimum number of swaps needed so that both resulting arrays are strictly increasing. Return -1 if it is impossible.

input_format.B: Integer array of the same length

questions.output_format: The minimum number of index-wise swaps, or -1 if no solution exists.

examples.explanation: Swapping the final pair produces [1,3,5,7] and [1,2,3,4].
One swap at index 1 makes both sequences strictly increasing.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: A one-element sequence is already strictly increasing.
No swaps are required.
The optimal choice may depend on the previous index state.
No index-wise swaps can make both sequences strictly increasing.
Strict comparisons must handle negative values.

questions.title: Burst Balloons for Maximum Coins
questions.problem_statement: You are given an array nums of non-negative balloon values. When balloon i is burst, you earn leftValue * nums[i] * rightValue, where leftValue and rightValue are the values of the nearest unburst balloons on either side, or 1 if no such balloon exists. Return the maximum coins obtainable by bursting every balloon.
questions.output_format: The maximum number of coins obtainable.

examples.explanation: An optimal bursting order earns 167 coins.
Bursting 1 first earns 5, then bursting 5 earns 5, for a total of 10.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: There is nothing to burst.
The two virtual boundary values are both 1.
The reward is zero.
Every burst earns one coin.
The optimal order accounts for the changing neighbors.

questions.title: Maximum Value of an Equation From Points
questions.problem_statement: You are given points sorted by strictly increasing x-coordinate. For a pair i < j satisfying x[j] - x[i] <= k, compute y[i] + y[j] + x[j] - x[i]. Return the maximum value over all valid pairs. At least one valid pair is guaranteed.

input_format.points: Array of [x, y] pairs sorted by strictly increasing x

questions.output_format: The maximum equation value among valid pairs.
constraints: At least one valid pair exists

examples.explanation: The first two points yield 3+0+(2-1)=4.
The pair [0,0] and [2,3] yields 0+3+2=5; [2,3] and [3,1] also yields 5.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The only pair determines the maximum.
The best equation value may be negative.
Pairs at the inclusive distance boundary are valid.
Expired points must not be used with a later point.
The expression needs 64-bit intermediate arithmetic.

questions.title: Minimum Refueling Stops
questions.problem_statement: A vehicle starts at position 0 with startFuel units of fuel. It consumes one unit of fuel per unit of distance and has an effectively unlimited tank. Given a target distance and fuel stations [position, fuel] sorted by position, return the minimum number of stops needed to reach the target, or -1 if it is impossible. At a station, any amount of its fuel may be taken, up to its available amount.
questions.output_format: The minimum number of refueling stops, or -1 if the target is unreachable.

examples.explanation: Refuel at positions 10 and 60 to reach the destination with two stops.
The vehicle cannot reach the first station.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No stops are required when initial fuel reaches the target.
The destination is unreachable.
A station at the exact reachable endpoint can be used.
Fuel from an unreachable station cannot be used.

edge_cases.case: Several stations but one is enough
edge_cases.why_it_matters: Choose the most useful previously passed station when fuel is needed.

questions.function_signature: minRefuelStops(target: integer, startFuel: integer, stations: integer[][]) -> integer

questions.title: Maximum Score After Pairing Numbers
questions.problem_statement: Given an array nums of even length 2n, perform n operations. In operation i (1-based), choose two remaining values at indices p and q, remove them, and earn i * gcd(nums[p], nums[q]) points. Return the maximum total score obtainable by choosing the pairs and their order optimally.

input_format.nums: Array of positive integers with even length

questions.output_format: The maximum total score.

examples.explanation: The only pair has gcd 1 and is used in operation 1.
Pairing 3 with 6 in operation 1 and 4 with 8 in operation 2 earns 3+8=11.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: The only gcd is 5.
Every pair has gcd 1, so the operation multipliers determine the total.
Each pair has gcd 4 and both operation multipliers contribute.
Pairing 2 with 6 for operation 1 and 4 with 8 for operation 2 earns 2 + 8 = 10.
The state space must remain feasible at the largest allowed length.

questions.expected_time_complexity: O(n^2 * 2^n), where n is the number of pairs (half the array length)

questions.title: Count Subarrays With Exactly K Distinct Values
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and a positive integer k, return the number of contiguous subarrays containing exactly k distinct values. Return the count as a 64-bit integer.

input_format.k: Positive target number of distinct values

questions.output_format: The number of subarrays with exactly k distinct values.

examples.explanation: Seven contiguous subarrays contain exactly two distinct values.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No non-empty subarray exists.
Every non-empty subarray contains at least one distinct value.
No subarray can contain three distinct values.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: Every non-empty subarray qualifies.

edge_cases.case: All values distinct with k one
edge_cases.why_it_matters: Only the four singleton subarrays qualify.

questions.title: Make an Array Strictly Increasing With Replacements
questions.problem_statement: Given arrays arr1 and arr2, you may replace any element of arr1 with any element from arr2. Each replacement costs one operation, and values from arr2 may be reused. Return the minimum number of replacements needed to make arr1 strictly increasing, or -1 if it is impossible.
questions.output_format: The minimum number of replacements, or -1 if impossible.

examples.explanation: Replacing 5 with 2 gives [1,2,3,6,7].
Two replacements are necessary to obtain a strictly increasing sequence.

edge_cases.why_it_matters: No replacement is required.
A single element is already strictly increasing.
The only available array is not strictly increasing.
The replacement options must be deduplicated or otherwise handled without overcounting.

questions.title: Minimum Removals to Form a Mountain Subsequence
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, remove as few elements as possible, without changing the order of the remaining elements, so that the remaining sequence is a mountain: it has at least three elements, strictly increases to one interior peak, then strictly decreases. questions.output_format: The minimum number of removals, or -1 if no valid mountain subsequence exists.

Strict inequalities prohibit a mountain.

questions.title: Maximum Points With Cost in a Grid
questions.problem_statement: Given an m by n integer matrix points, choose exactly one cell from each row. If column c is chosen in one row and column d in the next row, subtract abs(c-d) from the sum of chosen cell values. Return the maximum total score over all choices.
questions.output_format: The maximum achievable total score as a 64-bit integer.

questions.title: Minimum Number of K-Consecutive Bit Flips
questions.problem_statement: Given a binary array nums and a positive integer k, one operation flips exactly k consecutive bits (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0). Return the minimum number of operations needed to make every bit equal to 1, or -1 if it is impossible.
questions.output_format: The minimum number of flips, or -1 if no valid sequence of flips exists.

examples.explanation: Flip the first and third bits individually.

Every zero can be flipped independently.

questions.title: Minimize Deviation in an Array
questions.problem_statement: Given a non-empty array of positive integers, you may repeatedly halve an even value or double an odd value. Return the minimum possible difference between the maximum and minimum array values after any number of allowed operations.

questions.title: Maximum Balanced Subsequence Sum
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, choose a non-empty subsequence with indices i1 < i2 < ... such that nums[ij] - ij is non-decreasing across the chosen indices (using zero-based indices). Return the maximum possible sum of the chosen values.

questions.title: Maximum Total Reward With Increasing Choices
questions.problem_statement: You are given a multiset of positive integer reward values and start with a total reward of zero. questions.title: Count Ways to Split an Array Into Three Ordered Parts
questions.problem_statement: Given an array nums of non-negative integers, count the ways to split it into three non-empty contiguous parts with sums left, middle, and right such that left <= middle <= right. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.
